title: Implement lab_to_srgb conversion with gamut clipping report
description: Add the exact inverse of TASK-4 to `src/lumamatch/color.py`, converting CIELab float64 back to 8-bit sRGB. Because changing L* while holding a*/b* fixed can push colors outside the sRGB gamut, this function must also report what fraction of pixels required clipping so the CLI can surface it rather than hiding the loss.
acceptanceCriteria: `clipped_fraction` is the fraction of *pixels* (not channels) where any channel fell outside [0,1] before clipping, in [0.0, 1.0]
A deliberately out-of-gamut Lab value (e.g. L*=95 with a*=80, b*=-80) returns clipped_fraction > 0
Quantization uses round-half-away-from-zero, not NumPy's default banker's rounding
Round-tripping `srgb_to_lab` then `lab_to_srgb` over all 256 grey levels and 4096 random colors returns byte-identical uint8 values

steps.details: Write `_lab_f_inv(t)`: `np.where(t > DELTA, t ** 3, 3 * DELTA**2 * (t - 4/29))`. Note the threshold here is DELTA (not DELTA_CUBED) because the input is in f-space.
From L, a, b: `fy = (L + 16) / 116`, `fx = fy + a / 500`, `fz = fy - b / 200`. Apply `_lab_f_inv` to each, multiply componentwise by `D65_WHITE`, stack to (H,W,3).
Compute `XYZ_TO_SRGB = np.linalg.inv(SRGB_TO_XYZ)` once at module level (derive it rather than hardcoding, so the two matrices can never drift out of sync). Apply as `xyz @ XYZ_TO_SRGB.T`.

steps.description: Implement the forward sRGB transfer function
steps.details: Write `_linear_to_srgb(c)`: `np.where(c <= 0.0031308, c * 12.92, 1.055 * np.abs(c) ** (1/2.4) - 0.055)`. Use `np.abs` inside the power to avoid NaN on slightly negative out-of-gamut values; the sign is irrelevant because those values get clipped to 0 next.

After the transfer function and before clipping, build `out_of_range = (srgb < 0.0) | (srgb > 1.0)`, then `clipped_pixels = np.any(out_of_range, axis=-1)`. Set `clipped_fraction = float(clipped_pixels.mean())` (guard against zero-size arrays). Then `np.clip(srgb, 0.0, 1.0)`.

Use `np.floor(srgb * 255.0 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8)` for round-half-away-from-zero. Do NOT use `np.round`, which rounds halves to even and will break the byte-exact round-trip assertion. Values are already clipped so no overflow is possible.

Create `tests/test_color_inverse.py`: (a) all 256 greys round-trip byte-exact; (b) 4096 seeded random RGB triplets round-trip byte-exact; (c) in-gamut image gives clipped_fraction 0.0; (d) an array of L*=95, a*=80, b*=-80 gives clipped_fraction == 1.0; (e) ValueError on uint8 input and on shape (H,W,2).
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` (all prior tests must still pass) and `.venv/bin/ruff check src/lumamatch/color.py`.

technicalNotes: The byte-exact round-trip is the single most valuable test in this task — if it passes, both directions of the color math are almost certainly correct.
Deriving XYZ_TO_SRGB with np.linalg.inv rather than hardcoding it guarantees the inverse is exact to machine precision and eliminates a class of transcription typos.
clipped_fraction counts pixels, not channels, because that is the number a user can reason about ('0.02% of pixels were clipped').
The PRD specifies clip-only; do NOT implement chroma desaturation toward the gamut boundary. That was explicitly rejected as out of scope.
